q: The Blum-Shub-Smale (BSS) model of computation over ℝ (the real RAM model) can decide the Mandelbrot set membership problem in:
opts: Polynomial time over ℝ (using exact real arithmetic, Newton iteration converges geometrically)
exp: Over the BSS model (exact real arithmetic), Mandelbrot set membership is decidable in polynomial time: iterate z ↦ z²+c exactly and check if |z| > 2 within polynomially many steps. This contrasts with the classical Turing model where the boundary ∂M poses challenges.
